title: Stability tuner for hybrid FlashAttention integration and prefill scheduling optimizer
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Investigate and implement a runtime-level stability tuner that harmonizes FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernel selection during prefill and decode phases. The goal is to eliminate observed decode jitter and rare OOM regressions after v3 rollout, while preserving v3 performance uplift for long-context workloads. This ticket covers telemetry-driven policy design, compatibility shims, canary rollout strategy, and an optimizer to steer prefill scheduling based on recent kernel success rates and memory headroom.
background: During the v3 rollout in late Jan 2026 we observed intermittent decode latency spikes and two customer incidents where multitenant pods hit OOM during bursty long-context prefill activity. Initial root cause analysis points to a combination of v3 microtiling memory fragmentation and aggressive prefill coalescing that increases peak workspace usage. v2 remains stable but slower on long contexts. We need a mitigations-first approach that avoids model-owner changes and operates in the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry pipeline surfaces per-kernel success/failure, peak workspace per-request, and prefill vs decode workspace delta
A runtime shim can route to fallback kernel deterministically based on recent failure rate and memory headroom
Canary rollout (5% of traffic) shows <1% regression in latency tail and zero OOMs over 48h compared to control
Automated e2e replay tests reproduce previous OOM and confirm mitigation prevents it
Documentation and rollout runbook added to Console Ops playbook
investigation_notes: Reproduced decode spike locally with synthetic workload (batch=8, seq=8192) by interleaving small-prefill and then a large decode; v3 shows 18% higher peak workspace than v2 under microtile alignment mismatch
Heap snapshots indicate fragmentation in per-stream scratch allocator caused by variable tiling between prefill and decode phases
On-device profiling (nvprof/rocprof) shows v3 kernel launching additional workspace allocations when head-slicing increases at decode time

Hypothesis: sudden switch from cache-hot prefill to large decode tasks causes allocator to request fresh large segments that push tenant over quota — timing-sensitive, appears under bursty arrival patterns
proposed_solution: Implement 'kernel-stability-tuner' in runtime that tracks a sliding window of per-tenant kernel health metrics (failure_count, avg_workspace, peak_workspace)
Add deterministic fallback policy: if in last 5 minutes failure_rate > 1% OR estimated peak_workspace + request_estimate > tenant_memory_limit, route to v2-compatible kernel variant
Introduce prefill-aware preallocation: when prefill indicates imminent large decode (heuristics: prompt length + system message size), warm a reserved scratch buffer to avoid fragmentation
Expose feature flag to enable 'tuner' and a canary target percentage; include metrics for debugging in Console
Add scheduling hint: prefer v3 for long steady sequences where microtiling efficiency wins, prefer v2 for mixed prefill/decode bursts
tradeoffs_and_risks: Routing to v2 reduces tail latency benefits customers expect from v3 on long-context requests
Prefill preallocation increases short-term memory reservations which could slightly reduce overall consolidation density
Complex policy increases runtime code paths and maintenance surface; must be well-tested to avoid oscillation (kernel flip-flop)
Overaggressive fallbacks could hide upstream kernel bugs and delay permanent fixes
engineering_tasks: Add kernel health metrics to runtime telemetry (pull-request: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4567)
Implement stability-tuner module with Hysteresis and cooldown (branch: feature/kernel-tuner)
Integrate prefill preallocator and add unit tests for allocator invariants
Add canary rollout orchestration (Console + routing policy hookup)
Create synthetic e2e replay to reproduce OOM (artifact: drive.google.com/replication-playbook)
qa_and_validation: Run canary for 48h with production-synced replay at 5% traffic
Run stress test suites with multitenant consolidation at 90th percentile density
Add regression test to CI that runs micro-tiling matrix across seq lengths 512..8192
Manual verification of Console telemetry dashboards and alerts
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal canary (10 hosts) with feature flag enabled for dev orgs
Stage 2: gradual 1% -> 5% -> 25% traffic expansion with automated health checks (latency tail, OOMs, throughput)
Stage 3: full enable with 7d retention of augmented metrics and automated rollback on health degradation
